headline: Approved one-day wine and malt beverage permits for a Senior Center wedding reception and many events at The Break Bike Shop.
summary: Minutes from October 5, 2026 were also approved. A change of premises request for The Cellar, 14 Mill Street, was referred to a public hearing on November 2, 2026.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the October 5, 2026 regular meeting by roll call vote 2/0.
Approved a one-day wine and malt beverage permit for a wedding reception at the Senior Center, 14 Wallace Avenue, by unanimous roll call vote 2/0.
Approved one-day wine and malt beverage events at The Break Bike Shop, 880 Main Street, by unanimous roll call vote 2/0.
Referred the change of premises request for The Cellar, 14 Mill Street, to a public hearing on November 2, 2026.

MINUTES OF MEETING 
A regular meeting of the Board of License Commissioners was held on Monday, October 19, 2026, called to 
order by Commissioner Sarefield at 6:00 PM. Commissioner Boscardin was present. FPD Liaison Lt. 
Christopher Bellofatto was present and Officer Michael Sevigny. City Clerk Joanna Bilotta and Assistant City 
Clerk Elizabeth McNiff were present.  
I. REVIEW AND APPROVAL OF MINUTES OF PRIOR MEETING(S) 
Regular Minutes of October 5, 2026.  
The regular of October 5, 2026 were approved by roll call vote 2/0.  
 
II. NEW APPLICATIONS 
Please note that the Commission may enter into Executive Session pursuant to G.L. c. 30A, sec. 21(a) 
(5) (Discussion of CORI results), if required during this portion of the agenda, and will return to 
regular session upon completion. 
 
Special One Day Wine & Malt Beverages 
Agnes Hernandez, Senior Center, 14 Wallace Avenue, Wedding Reception, Saturday, December 5, 
2026, from 4:00 PM – 10:00 PM for approximately 200 people.   
Ms. Hernandez was present at the meeting VIA zoom. Commissioner Sarefield reviewed the application 
and verified that the event will have TIP certified servers. Ms. Hernandez explained that this was her 
wedding reception, there would be a licensed bartender checking ID’s where they would be serving 
alcohol. Commissioner Sarefield stated that all serving of alcohol must be ceased thirty minutes prior 
to closing.  
No concerns from Lt. Bellofatto. 
Applications approved by unanimous roll call vote 2/0.  
 
Josh Merchant, The Break Bike Shop, 880 Main Street, Thursday, November 5th, 12th, 19, 2026, 
Thursday, December 3rd, 10th, 17th, and 31, 2026 from 4:00 PM – 11:30 PM for approximately 30 
people.   
Josh Merchant, The Break Bike Shop, 880 Main Street, Friday, November 6th, 13th, 20th, 27, 2026, 
Friday, December 4th, 11th, 18th, and 25, 2026 from 4:00 PM – 11:30 PM for approximately 30 people.
Page 2 
 
 
Josh Merchant, The Break Bike Shop, 880 Main Street, Saturday, October 31, 2026, Saturday, 
November 7th, 14th, 21st, 28, 2026, Saturday, December 5th, 12th, 19th, 26th and 31, 2026 from 4:00 PM – 
11:30 PM for approximately 30 people.   
Josh Merchant, The Break Bike Shop, 880 Main Street, Sunday, November 29, 2026 from 4:00 PM – 
11:30 PM for approximately 30 people.   
Mr. Merchant was present at the meeting and explained to the Commission that the events he was 
planning to hold would be small in scale and would take place prior to his submission of a liquor license 
application. Commissioner Sarefield confirmed that Mr. Merchant was TIP certified, which Mr. 
Merchant affirmed. He also stated that his father-in-law, who is also TIP certified, would be assisting 
him with the events. Commissioner Sarefield reminded Mr. Merchant that all alcohol service must cease 
thirty minutes prior to closing. Commissioner Sarefield also expressed concern that the existing liquor 
license associated with the property remained tied to the location. City Clerk Joanna Bilotta confirmed 
with Mr. Merchant that the previous tenant had no alcohol stored at the premises. Ms. Bilotta explained 
that a similar situation had occurred at 326 Main Street, where Mr. Craig was permitted to hold special 
one day events while Mr. Gregory maintained a pocket license associated with the location. Mr. 
Gregory ultimately did not renew his liquor license for that location. 
No concerns from Lt. Bellofatto. 
Applications approved by unanimous roll call vote 2/0.  
Application for Amendment- Change or Alteration of Premises  
Ziggymill33, LLC / DBA The Cellar, 14 Mill Street 
(Refer to Public Hearing Monday, November 2, 2026.)

Joanna Bilotta, City Clerk
